pr_title: fix: exclude missing dependencies from optimization during SSR
pr_body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing! -->

### Description

<!-- Please insert your description here and provide especially info about the "what" this PR is solving -->

Optimized based on #4904 , fixed #4700 , and added test cases.

After I submitted the RP #4904 , I am going to add test cases according to the comment of @patak-js .
 
In the process of building test cases, I found a problem.

For testing, I did not add the script entry point in the `index.html`, it will be dynamically added during SSR.

First, if you import a missing dependency that contains multiple entries during SSR, it will execute `server._registerMissingImport` and build a server-based output.

Then, when the client imports the same missing dependency that contains multiple entries, it will directly consume the build result of the SSR stage. The build result is only applicable to the server, and importing on the client will cause an error.

In my opinion, there is no need to execute `server._registerMissingImport` during the SSR, because the build result is based on the server, and the optimized dependencies are for the client.

If there is anything missing, please remind me.

This only happens during the `optimize missing deps` phase of the dev server.

comments:
This error occurs because `esbuildDepPlugin` incorrectly resolve the built-in module:

https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/e623b4a34878d8f2a88f515ea798d814790742ee/packages/vite/src/node/optimizer/esbuildDepPlugin.ts#L113-L131

Vite's own resolver will return the built-in module id, the id will be resolved by `path.resolve(resolve)`, and the result is:
`/project/path/built-in-module-id`

The resolved content is wrong, we need to externalize the built-in module during SSR, modify the source code:

```js
  if (isExternalUrl(resolved) || (ssr && isBuiltin(id))) {
    return {
      path: resolved,
      external: true
    }
  }
```

So the esbuild will resolve the correct content. I will submit a pull request later.

```
Error: Failed to resolve import "fs/promises" from "components/problematic/render.jsx". Does the file exist?
    at formatError (/sandbox/node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/dep-55830a1a.js:42190:46)

    at async TransformContext.transform (/sandbox/node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/dep-55830a1a.js:67341:57)
    at async Object.transform (/sandbox/node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/dep-55830a1a.js:42397:30)

```

With `vite/2.6.5 linux-x64 node-v14.17.6`

After spending some time digging the source code, I assumed that this is a vite bug, and the bug has nothing to do with this PR.

In the SSR phase, using ssrLoaderModule will trigger the `resolveId` hook of the `resolve` plugin. The call stack is like `ssrLoaderModule -> transformRequest -> pluginContainer.transform -> importAnalysis.transform -> resolve.resolveId`.

In the hook, use the `utils.isBuiltin` function to determine whether it is a built-in module, it does not consider the case of deep import (e.g. "fs/promises"), resulting in a resolving error.

https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/b17444fd97b02bc54410c8575e7d3cb25e4058c2/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/resolve.ts#L244-L246

https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/b17444fd97b02bc54410c8575e7d3cb25e4058c2/packages/vite/src/node/utils.ts#L40-L42

Change the source code to the following to fix it

```js
export function isBuiltin(id: string): boolean {
  const deepMatch = id.match(deepImportRE)
  id = deepMatch ? deepMatch[1] || deepMatch[2] : id
  return builtins.includes(id)
}
``` 

I will submit a PR to fix it soon :)
